headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading errors: haystack’s MCP/networked retrieval can feed xonsh’s shell/filesystem actions without verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: haystack can call MCP servers and broad network egress, so it may ingest untrusted content; xonsh can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, making it plausible that retrieved content is treated as instructions. No shared channel is explicit, so this is inferred rather than directly documented.
conditions: IF haystack forwards retrieved text into xonsh command input without sanitization
IF an MCP server returns attacker-controlled content that xonsh interprets as shell syntax
mitigations: Disable automatic command execution from retrieved text
Require explicit human approval before xonsh runs generated commands
Restrict haystack MCP sources to trusted servers
Add allowlist validation for shell metacharacters
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from retrieval to execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: haystack has broad network egress and MCP access, while xonsh reads and writes filesystem contents and environment variables. If they share a workspace or pass files through the same environment, sensitive local data can be retrieved and then exfiltrated by haystack. The shared-workspace path is plausible but not proven, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem tree
IF haystack is configured to send retrieved file contents to external APIs or MCP endpoints
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Block haystack from reading local secrets directories
Limit xonsh access to non-sensitive files
Review outbound destinations for haystack
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: haystack can use MCP and broad network egress, and xonsh can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. Even without modify_git_state, both can mutate shared resources if pointed at the same directory or service, creating race conditions and conflicting writes in default-like setups. Uncertainty about orchestration locking keeps this at high rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same writable directory or remote resource
IF no external lock or transaction layer serializes their writes
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run only one writer at a time
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Disable write access for one agent during the other's run
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: haystack can produce retrieved answers or tool outputs, and xonsh can act on shell commands and filesystem changes. If xonsh treats haystack output as authoritative, a bad retrieval or hallucinated instruction can cascade into destructive local actions. The pairwise pathway is plausible from the profiles, and the lack of verification makes the blast radius high.
conditions: IF xonsh consumes haystack output without a verification step
IF haystack output is converted into shell commands or file edits
mitigations: Insert a human review step before execution
Require xonsh to validate commands against a policy
Log and diff all proposed file changes
Use dry-run mode for shell actions
requires-engineering: add schema validation for haystack outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and only explicitly touch anonymous usage statistics, shell commands, filesystem contents, source code, configuration, environment variables, and notebooks. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to generic logging or local-data handling gaps rather than a specific violation.
conditions: IF either deployment logs sensitive local files or environment variables beyond the documented data classes
IF a deployment policy requires residency or certification guarantees not present in the profiles
mitigations: Minimize logged data fields
Avoid placing regulated data in shared workspaces
Review retention settings for both agents
Document data-class handling in deployment notes
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
